result.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens, the credential-sync branch returns the raw `fetch` Response. In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff changes to `const token = res?.data;` — a fetch Response has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` on the next line throws a TypeError. Previously the destructured `{ res }` came from myGoogleAuth.refreshToken whose res had `.data`. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff; the finding is accurate.

judged_text: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint, and this code reads `res?.data` (undefined on a Response, the body is never .json()-parsed) then dereferences `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError on every refresh. Every Google Calendar token refresh in a credential-sharing deployment throws TypeError, so calendar sync fails for all users as soon as access tokens expire (~hourly).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, it does `const response = await fetch(...)` and returns that raw Fetch `Response`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` then does `const token = res?.data;` and immediately dereferences `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date`. A Fetch `Response` has no `.data` property, so `token` will be `undefined` and this will throw at runtime whenever the sync-endpoint branch is used.
